questions.q: Phenol is shaken with benzoyl chloride and aqueous NaOH. The product is:
questions.explain: In NaOH phenol is present as phenoxide, which attacks the acid chloride to give the ester C₆H₅COOC₆H₅.

questions.q: Which amine does NOT undergo benzoylation under Schotten–Baumann conditions?
questions.explain: Acylation replaces a hydrogen on nitrogen; a tertiary amine such as N,N-dimethylaniline has no N–H and cannot form an amide.

questions.q: What is the main role of aqueous NaOH in the Schotten–Baumann reaction?
options: It neutralises the HCl formed, so the amine is not protonated and stays nucleophilic
It hydrolyses the acid chloride to the acid, which then reacts
It converts the amine into an amide ion before attack
It acts as the acylating agent
questions.explain: Without base, HCl would convert the remaining amine into R–NH₃⁺, which has no free lone pair; removing HCl also drives the reaction forward.

questions.q: Why is benzoyl chloride, rather than benzoic acid, used to benzoylate an amine at room temperature?
options: Benzoic acid is not soluble in NaOH
Benzoic acid gives an ester with amines
A carboxylic acid simply forms a salt with the amine at room temperature
Benzoic acid hydrolyses faster than benzoyl chloride
questions.explain: Carboxylic acids and amines undergo acid–base reaction to a salt rather than acyl substitution, so the acid chloride is used.
